newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields up awaiting US data barrage.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields up awaiting US data barrage.

text.p: *Australian debt yields closed higher as the market corrected the recent strong rally to 3-1/4 year lows ahead of a barrage of U.S. data later on Tuesday.
*RBA easing now seen more likely around July board meeting.
Australian debt yields closed higher as the market corrected the recent strong rally to 3-1/4 year lows, taking the opportunity to book profits ahead of a barrage of U.S. data later on Tuesday.

"We have had a very strong rally over the course of the past few sessions, so we have seen the market pullback a little, which is not surprising," said Stephen Roberts, chief economist at UBS Australia. "There is also probably a little bit of nervousness running into all that data out of the U.S."
The U.S. releases CPI, housing starts, industrial production and capacity utilisation for May.
Long-dated bond yields crept back over 7.0 percent, while short-dated yields and bill futures gave up some of the bullish tone as the Reserve Bank stayed silent on monetary policy.

However, September bill futures at 94.83 are still indicating a cash rate of 5.17 percent, well below current 5.5 percent official interest rates and despite today's easier tone. Analysts now believe that the RBA will be more likely ease policy around the time of the July 1 board meeting and the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on July 1 and 2, which will also coincide with the market's next major data, the retail trade report for May.

The local corrective tone saw spread differentials widen against the dollar bloc after the recent strong outperformance. The yield curve also flattened after spiking sharply last week after a weak labour force report, which fuelled expectations of a further monetary policy easing.
